 : Judgment :
Heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for the respondents.

2. The appellant insurance company has filed this appeal challenging the liability and to set aside the judgment and award dated 16.11.2011 passed in MVC.No.12/2011 by the learned Senior Civil Judge & MACT, Gangavathi.
3. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as they are referred to in the claim petition before the Tribunal.

4. Brief facts of the claimant's case before the Tribunal are as under:
The claimant was the driver of Maruti Omni Car bearing registration No.KA.37/M-2395, who met with an accident on 05.07.2010, when he was proceeding to Kottal from Kampli along with his friends in aforesaid vehicle, when the said vehicle came on Kampli Kottal road, near Muruli krishna Rice Mill at Kampli,
the clement being the driver of the Car drove the same in care and caution on the left side of the road, at NC: 2024:KHC-D:9866 that time some cattle suddenly came in-front of the vehicle, due to which, the claimant avoided the possible accident, but the vehicle turned toward left side of the road and thus the claimant lost his control over the vehicle and the dashed to one culvert and accordingly caused the accident.
Due to the said impact, the claimant sustained injuries.
Immediately he was shifted to Government Hospital, Kampli for treatment, when the first informant lodged the complaint.
This led to registration of FIR and investigation.
5. Considering the oral and documentary evidence and record, the Tribunal awarded a compensation of Rs.71,000.
Hence, the insurance company has filed this appeal.
6. Learned counsel for the Insurance company contended that, the tribunal has wrongly entertained the claim petition and passed the impugned award.
The accident in question caused due to negligence and default under wrongful act of claimant.

The police have filed charge sheet against claimant for his rash and negligent driving, but the tribunal has not considered these aspect and has not NC: 2024:KHC-D:9866 considered that, the accident was due to wrongful act of owner of the The Senior Branch Manager vs Basavaraj S/O Somanna on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14207441/
2 vehicle.

entities.text: Senior Branch Manager vs Basavaraj S/O Somanna
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence the claim petition filed by the owner is barred under section 163-A of the M.V.Act.

The Tribunal has not considered the ratio laid down in the case of the National Insurance Co. Ltd.
Vs. Sinitha and others1 and Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Sharada G and others2.

National Insurance Co. Ltd.
Vs. Sinitha and others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Sharada G and others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further the Tribunal has not considered the aspect that there is violation of policy condition as the driver of the vehicle was not holding driving license for a transport vehicle which amounts to violation of policy condition.
Hence the learned counsel prayed to allow the appeal.

7. Learned counsel for the claimant submits that the Tribunal considering oral and documentary evidence has rightly awarded compensation, which do not require any interference, hence prayed to dismiss the appeal.

8. After hearing both the parties, the points that would arise for Court's consideration are as follows:
i. Whether the insurance company-appellant proved that, the claimant himself tortfeasor, due to his 2012 ACJ 1 2010 ACJ 977 NC: 2024:KHC-D:9866 negligence,
the accident occurred hence the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation.
ii.
Whether the compensation awarded by the tribunal is just unreasonable or does it call for reduction?

9. It is the contention of the insurance company that the claimant himself negligent in the accident thus, he sustained injuries due to his own negligence and hence petition of claimant is not maintainable.
10.
In order to substantiate this contention, RW.1 was examined on oath and reiterating the contention as taken in the appeal.

11. On the contrary, the claimant relied upon Ex.P.1- FIR, Ex.P.2-Charge sheet, Ex.P.3-Panchanama,
Ex.P.4- Wound Certificate and Ex.P.8-D.L, Ex.P.9-R.C. and Ex.P.10- Insurance Policy.
They establish that the Investigating Officer filed charge sheet against the claimant and the contents of Ex.P.4-Wound Certificate indicates that, the claimant sustained grievous injuries.
From the perusal of Ex.P.8, rider of Car possessed valid and effective driving licence and he was permitted to drive Light Motor Vehicle.

In the case of Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited and others3,
wherein, the Hon'ble Apex Court was of the opinion that, if a person possess LMV driving licence, he can drive light motor vehicle unladen weight less than 7,500 Kgs.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited and others3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the instant case, the claimant drove Maruti Omni Vehicle which was less than 7,500/- Kgs., i.e., 1,100/- Kgs.
13.
Hence, it is just and necessary to peruse Section 163-A M.V.Act, "163A. Special provisions as to payment of compensation on structured formula basis.

The Senior Branch Manager vs Basavaraj S/O Somanna on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14207441/
3 (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or in any other law for the time being in force or instrument having the force of law, the owner of the motor vehicle of the authorised insurer shall be liable to pay in the case of death or permanent disablement due to accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle, compensation, as indicated in the Second Schedule, to the legal heirs or the victim, as the case may be.
Explanation.--For the purposes of this sub- section, "permanent disability" shall have the same (2016) 4 SCC 298 NC: 2024:KHC-D:9866 meaning and extent as in the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 (8 of 1923).

entities.text: Senior Branch Manager vs Basavaraj S/O Somanna on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (2) In any claim for compensation under sub- section (1), the claimant shall not be required to plead or establish that the death or permanent disablement in respect of which the claim has been made was due to any wrongful act or neglect or default of the owner of the vehicle or vehicles concerned or of any other person.
(3) The Central Government may, keeping in view the cost of living by notification in the Official Gazette, from time to time amend the Second Schedule."

14. From the perusal of the aforesaid proposition, Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act, provided for payment of compensation on structured formula basis by mandating that the owner of a motor vehicle or the authorized insurer would be liable to pay compensation, as indicated in the second schedule in the case of death or permanent disability due to accident arising out of the use of the motorcycle, to the legal heirs or the victim, as the case may be in a claim made under sub Section (1)
of Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act.

In order to prove a claim of this nature, the claimant need not be required to plead or NC: 2024:KHC-D:9866 establish that the death or permanent disablement in respect of which the claim has been made was due to any wrongful act or negligent or default of the owner of the vehicle concerned.
In the instant case, the claimant drove the maruti omni vehicle and caused the accident.
15. The Hon'ble apex Court in the case of Chandrakanth Tiwari Vs.
New India
Assurance Company Limited
and another4 has held as follows:
HELD: The claimant need not plead or establish that the death in respect of which the claim was made, was due to any negligence or default of the owner of the vehicle or of any other person.
(emphasis supplied).

It is not relevant that the person insured must be the driver of the vehicle but may well have been riding with somebody else driving a vehicle which resulted in the death of the person driving the vehicle.

The High Court is clearly wrong in stating that it was necessary under Section 163-A to prove that somebody else was driving the vehicle rashly and negligently, as a result of which, the death of the victim would take place.
(2020) 5 SCR 868 NC: 2024:KHC-D:9866 The Senior Branch Manager vs Basavaraj S/O Somanna on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14207441/
4 16.

entities.text: Senior Branch Manager vs Basavaraj S/O Somanna
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A perusal of this provision would show that the claimant need not plead or establish that the injuries in respect of which the claim was made was due to any negligence or default of the rider or owner of the vehicle.
In this view of the matter, it is not relevant that the person insured must be the driver of the vehicle.
17. Insofar as quantum of compensation is concerned, this petition was filed under Section 163-A of M.V.Act, the compensation has to be worked out as per strict application of II-Schedule of M.V.Act.
The Tribunal considering the nature of injuries has granted a sum of Rs.5,000/- towards pain and suffering, which is reasonable one and hence no interference is called for in this head.

18. The Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.6,000/- towards loss of earning during medical treatment,
which is not permissible under Section 163-A of M.V.Act.
19.

The Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.3,000/- towards medical expenses , which is reasonable and no interference is called for in this regard.
- 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:9866 20.
The Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.54,000/- towards loss of future earnings, which is reasonable and hence, no interference is called for in this regard.

21. The Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.3,000/- towards conveyance, food and nourishment and attendant charges, which the claimant is not entitle under the M.V.Act.
22.

Hence, a sum of Rs.6,000/- and Rs.3,000/- towards loss of income during treatment and towards conveyance, food and nourishment and attendant charges respectively reduced out of sum of Rs.71,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
23. Hence, the claimant is entitled for compensation sum of Rs.62,000/- only.

Hence, I pass the following:
: ORDER :
i.
The appeal filed by the Insurance Company is allowed in part.
ii. The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is reduced from Rs.71,000/- to Rs.62,000/-.

Hence, the claimant is entitled for total compensation of Rs.62,000/-
with interest at - 11 - The Senior Branch Manager vs Basavaraj S/O Somanna on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14207441/
5 NC: 2024:KHC-D:9866 the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of its realization.

iv. On deposit, the entire compensation amount shall be disbursed to the claimant on proper identification v.
The amount in deposit shall be transmitted to the Tribunal.
No order as to costs.
